subject.title: Low-risk: Docker Go template injection, thread-ownership URL path injection, TLS env bypass

question: Should OpenClaw keep the current private-DNS WebSocket and Control UI dangerous break-glass behavior, narrow it with a new explicit allowlist policy, or remove those bypasses?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally preserve these operator-selected risky paths, so changing them is a security boundary and compatibility decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Narrow with explicit policy
options.body: Add or define a stricter allowlist-style policy for private WebSocket names and dangerous Control UI bypasses, then land the Docker/thread encoding fixes alongside focused tests and docs.

options.title: Keep current break-glass behavior
options.body: Accept the existing documented operator-controlled bypasses and only fix the narrow Docker label validation and thread URL encoding issues.

options.title: Remove broad bypasses
options.body: Fail closed for private-DNS ws:// hostnames and dangerous Control UI flags, with release notes and migration guidance for affected operators.

recommendation.title: Narrow with explicit policy
recommendation.body: Add or define a stricter allowlist-style policy for private WebSocket names and dangerous Control UI bypasses, then land the Docker/thread encoding fixes alongside focused tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc merged the current private-WebSocket policy PR and is the strongest history signal for the Gateway compatibility/security decision.
